GitHub: Container Registry ​

Verified against primary documentation on 2026-10-16.

Where the documentation is silent, the fact below was observed with read-only, anonymous calls to ghcr.io and is marked as observed, not documented.

Names ​

The documented push form is docker push ghcr.io/NAMESPACE/IMAGE_NAME:latest, where NAMESPACE is "the name of the personal account or organization to which you want the image to be scoped" (Working with the Container registry). The owner is the only part of the path GitHub imposes.

Nested names are not discussed in the documentation. The pull example there only shows ghcr.io/NAMESPACE/IMAGE_NAME/release:1.14.1. Observed, anonymous tags/list calls succeed for names with four segments after the owner, so the depth of mirrors/docker-hub/library/postgres is confirmed:

NameSegments after the owner
tektoncd/catalog/upstream/tasks/git-clone4
defenseunicorns/packages/uds/bundles/k3d-core-demo4
homebrew/core/openssl/33
stefanprodan/charts/podinfo2

No maximum depth is documented, so a deeper limit is not known.

Lowercase is not stated on the pages above. The only primary source found is the docker/build-push-action troubleshooting guide, which says an image name built from github.repository fails when the repository contains uppercase letters, and fixes it by lowercasing the whole path (Troubleshooting). Observed, a request for stefanprodan/charts/Podinfo returns 404, while one with the owner written Stefanprodan resolves, so the owner is matched without regard to case and the name is not. Whether a push of an uppercase name is rejected was not tested, because that needs authentication.

The pages above do not say outright that a push creates the package. They say "When you first publish a package, the default visibility is private", which implies the first publish creates it. Visibility is then a setting of each package, not of the owner. A package pushed from the command line is not linked to a repository: "When you push a container image from the command line, the image is not linked to a repository by default." A workflow that publishes it links the repository that contains the workflow automatically.

To link a repository from the command line, add the label org.opencontainers.image.source to the image, as in LABEL org.opencontainers.image.source=https://github.com/OWNER/REPO (Connecting a repository to a package). A linked package shows the repository's README on its landing page, and "automatically inherits the access permissions of the linked repository" unless the organization has turned that inheritance off.

Tag immutability ​

No setting exists. The Container registry documentation and the Packages overview are silent on immutability, and no page describing such a setting was found. The only related source found is an open feature request in the GitHub community, Immutable image tags in container registry. Absence of a documented setting is the evidence here, so the ADR's statement that ghcr.io has none is consistent with the documentation but cannot be proven from it.

Retention ​

The documentation describes no cleanup policy and no automatic retention. The only time-based rule is for restoring: a deleted package or version can be restored "within 30 days of its deletion", if the namespace and version are not reused (Deleting and restoring a package).

Deletion is manual or scripted:

  • The REST API lists versions with GET /orgs/{org}/packages/{package_type}/{package_name}/versions and deletes one with DELETE /orgs/{org}/packages/{package_type}/{package_name}/versions/{package_version_id}. The delete call needs the read:packages and delete:packages scopes for tokens that use scopes (REST API for packages).
  • A workflow can delete with its GITHUB_TOKEN, "The token must have admin permission to the package."
  • A public package version with more than 5,000 downloads cannot be deleted through the API, and GitHub support must be contacted.
  • The package type for container images is container. The actions/delete-package-versions action takes package-type as docker (v4 or older) or container (v5 or newer), keeps the latest versions with min-versions-to-keep, and has delete-only-untagged-versions for container packages. Its README says "we are not taking contributions to this repository at this time."

The list response carries metadata.container.tags, an array of the tags on each version. Targeting pr- and 0.0.0-pr- tags is therefore done by listing versions, selecting those whose tags all start with one of the prefixes, and deleting them by package_version_id. The action has no tag-prefix filter. Its ignore-versions input is documented as "Takes regex for the version name", and a container version is named by its digest, so selecting on tags is a script over the REST API, not a setting of the action (the action's matching against container tags was not tested). A version that carries both a pr- tag and a release tag must be left alone, which the selection above handles by requiring every tag to match.

The REST documentation does not say how a package name that contains / is written in the path, and a search found nothing either. Standard URL encoding would write %2F, but this was not verified because it needs a token.

Mirrors ​

ghcr.io has no pull-through cache or remote repository feature in the pages above, and none was found elsewhere in the GitHub documentation. A mirror is a copy pushed by us. crane copy SRC DST does it, described as "Efficiently copy a remote image from src to dst while retaining the digest value", with --all-tags to copy every tag and --platform to restrict a multi-platform image (crane copy). Keeping the digest is what lets a deployment pin a mirror by digest. The documentation of crane copy mentions no flag for referrers, so signatures and attestations are not copied by it, and a tool that copies them is needed where they matter. That tool was not tested here.

Signatures and referrers ​

Observed, the repository stefanprodan/charts/podinfo holds, next to each version tag such as 6.3.4, a tag of the form sha256-<digest>.sig. The digest is that of the signed manifest: the manifest tagged 6.3.4 has digest sha256:8f513021... and the repository has a tag sha256-8f513021....sig whose manifest is an OCI manifest with a layer of media type application/vnd.dev.cosign.simplesigning.v1+json and the annotation dev.cosignproject.cosign/signature. So cosign signatures live in the same repository as the artifact, under a tag, and they are not separate packages. The same .sig tags appear in cloudnative-pg/charts/cloudnative-pg, home-operations/charts-mirror/cilium and sigstore/cosign/cosign.

A tag listing of such a repository therefore mixes release tags with signature tags. A cleanup script that deletes by tag must not treat .sig tags as releases, and must delete a signature with the version it describes.

The documentation says nothing about the OCI referrers API. Observed, GET /v2/<name>/referrers/<digest> on stefanprodan/charts/podinfo returns 404 with MANIFEST_UNKNOWN, both for a made-up digest and for the real digest of 6.3.4. The OCI Distribution Specification expects a registry that implements the API to answer 200 with an empty index when nothing refers to the digest, and tells clients to fall back to a tag derived from the digest when the response is 404 (OCI Distribution Specification). So ghcr.io was observed not to serve the referrers API on 2026-10-16, and signatures there are found by tag, not by referrers. This is a snapshot of behavior GitHub does not document and may change.

Helm charts ​

helm push takes a reference that "must be prefixed with oci:// and must not contain the basename or tag". The basename "is inferred from the chart's name" and the tag "is inferred from the chart's semantic version", which Helm calls "a strict requirement" (Helm: Use OCI-based registries). So helm push api-1.4.0.tgz oci://ghcr.io/<owner>/charts/shop publishes ghcr.io/<owner>/charts/shop/api:1.4.0. Helm's page has no ghcr.io push example, and says of helm registry login that the host is given without a scheme or a path. The same layout is observed in public use at ghcr.io/stefanprodan/charts/podinfo and ghcr.io/cloudnative-pg/charts/cloudnative-pg.

The Container registry documentation does not mention Helm charts. It lists "Open Container Initiative (OCI) Specifications" as a supported format (Working with the Container registry).
